recipe: Call t3.toTSL with a TypeGPU function to convert it into a TSL node that can be assigned to material properties or composed with other TSL nodes.
trigger_condition: When you need to plug TypeGPU shader logic into a Three.js material property.
evidence: Calling `t3.toTSL` with a TypeGPU function will return a TSL node, which can then be plugged into material properties, or used by other nodes.

recipe: Be aware that @typegpu/three makes your app only work on WebGPU-enabled devices, with no WebGL fallback, so consider your target audience's hardware support.
trigger_condition: When building a Three.js app that must run on a broad range of devices, including older GPUs without WebGPU support.
evidence: If your end user's device doesn't support WebGPU, Three.js enables a WebGL fallback. Currently, using @typegpu/three makes your app only work on WebGPU-enabled devices.

recipe: Write control flow in your TypeGPU shader code using familiar JavaScript syntax (if statements, for loops) instead of TSL special functions.
trigger_condition: When writing conditional logic or iteration in your shader code.
evidence: Control-flow like `if` statements and `for` loops makes use of familiar JavaScript syntax instead of special functions.

recipe: Unit-test your shader functions on the CPU before deploying them to the GPU to verify correctness.
trigger_condition: When you want to verify the correctness of your shader logic without a GPU.
evidence: Unit-testability, since you can call these functions on the CPU
